response_summary: Verified the current NOVA workforce mapping and repaired desktop-validation push targeting for 02-NOVA, updated desktop branch ownership documentation, and added a regression test; PR #76 opened with exact-head CI pending.

Hardened desktop settings startup against excessive JSON nesting by converting parser recursion failures into safe recovery errors; added a 10,000-level regression test proving the invalid source remains unchanged and explicit reset recovers; documented the behavior and verified 83 desktop tests plus unified and release validation on code head c7333946ccd28815ef3ba61a036934babb99a4cd.

Improved settings recovery UX by disabling all preference groups while the stored settings require recovery, preserving the separately confirmed Restore defaults action, and restoring editability after reset. Added a UI regression test and updated recovery documentation. Exact code head 1b7989e021faf168f241c18f20b4de4df926788a passed 84 desktop tests plus desktop push/PR, unified and release-manifest validation.

Closed a desktop settings coverage gap with a Qt backend recovery round-trip test: invalid preferences reject edits without rewriting the source, explicit reset clears recovery, and later edits persist. Updated settings documentation and PR #76; exact code head d2a88e46065b50d18dec4382dbf632fa188ca767 passed 85 desktop tests in push and PR workflows, unified validation and release-manifest validation.

Eliminated inconsistent startup validation by making SettingsController parse the bounded no-follow settings document once and apply migration plus validation to that same snapshot. Added a regression asserting one file open and documented the invariant. Exact code head e3c1d6b2b3c122b19a0c54b90ca057737ba7f556 passed 86 desktop tests in push and PR workflows, all 10 unified validation jobs and release-manifest integrity.

Fixed a settings-startup crash when JSON nesting is accepted by the parser but exceeds the migration deepcopy recursion budget. Migration now returns a bounded recovery error; regression tests cover the real nested-document path and deterministic deepcopy failure, and docs explain the behavior. Exact code head 4f36e8ad8e90d902811985367eaacc892e42c113 passed 88 desktop tests, all 10 unified validation jobs and release-manifest integrity.

Closed a transactional recovery gap with regression tests proving failed settings resets preserve the original on-disk document, current in-memory preferences, and recovery lock. Added controller and Qt SettingsBackend failure-path coverage and documented the guarantee. Exact PR head 225b09af140d999101c0d5f05932e6c2df7ab2c2 passed 91 desktop tests including the actual Qt offscreen QML runtime test, all 10 unified validation jobs and release-manifest integrity.

Fixed a settings persistence failure gap: if parent-directory fsync fails after atomic replacement, save_settings now restores the previous directory entry before returning failure. Added file-level and controller recovery-lock regression tests, updated persistence docs, and verified 93 desktop tests, all 10 unified validation jobs, and release-manifest integrity on code head 2499ee4834d06cb984895db8a2f5df5c83fe905f.

Added a regression test proving explicit settings recovery restores the original symlink itself when parent-directory fsync fails after atomic replacement; verified the symlink target and valid target JSON remain untouched and temporary/backup files are cleaned up. Desktop validation passed 94 tests, unified validation passed all 10 jobs, and release-manifest integrity passed on code head 56f686620a60a121dd6e7c8f06e770eaaf6d3f9a.

Completed a focused desktop/session/settings audit: re-verified the tested code head and PR #76 state, inspected session launcher, settings controller and persistence, migrations, Qt host and QML recovery behavior, and documented the remaining release gates without claiming unrun Fedora graphical or interactive accessibility acceptance.

Strengthened the parent-directory-fsync rollback regression: the prior settings fixture is now valid JSON, and the test confirms rollback restores a parseable document with the original panel.icon_size value. Desktop push and PR validation passed 94 tests, unified validation passed all 10 jobs, and PHOENIX release-manifest integrity passed on tested code head 33b60b4472db3a1bcba079fb8b74f4bac20d938a; PR #76 was updated with exact-head evidence.

Audited the standalone settings recovery CLI and Plasma session launcher/test coverage, found no additional safe code change that could be validated without the Fedora runtime dependencies, and synchronized PR #76 to the latest independently validated rollback-test code head while preserving the explicit Fedora graphical and accessibility acceptance gates.

Audited the Fedora 44 Plasma session package handoff against the current ATLAS manifest and desktop session requirements; confirmed that the package owning /usr/bin/startplasma-wayland is not yet evidenced by the selected repository snapshot, so no speculative manifest change was made. Posted an actionable repoquery/NEVRA/file-ownership evidence request to ATLAS issue #12 and retained the Fedora runtime acceptance gate.
